Tile = 64 tokens (gemm0CtaTileNbTokens) = 4 pages. headElems=128 → cacheHeadNbParts=2 (64-elem parts, 128 B swizzle rows). gmma::instM=64, instNBase=8, instK=16 (bf16). Gemm0Acc = GmmaAcc<64,8> = 1x1 core mat = 4 floats/thread; Gemm1Acc = GmmaAcc<128,8> = 2x1 = 8 floats/thread. wgmma shape everywhere: m64n8k16.f32.bf16.bf16 (gmma_impl.cuh has 12 bf16 specializations of it).

CTA: 640 threads = 5 warp groups, blockDim {128,1,5}; __launch_bounds__(640,2) → 48 regs/thread; setmaxnreg: z==2 (IO) dec 24, z>=3 (converters) inc 56, gemm groups stay 48 (128*24+256*56+256*48 = 29696 <= 30720; 1024 regs/CTA unallocated).
 z=0 gemm0 (4 warps), z=1 gemm1 (4), z=2 IO (warp0 Q load; warp0 K loader; warp1 V loader; warps 2-3 idle after prologue), z=3 K converters (4 warps, one per page), z=4 V converters.

SMEM (110.6 KB measured; my sum ~108 KB + 1 KB alignment): k[3 stages x 2 parts] 6 x 8 KB = 48 KB (alignas 1024); vBufs[3] x 16 KB = 48 KB; reusedXVOutSwizzleBuf[nbXBuf=2] = union{XBuffer 8x8 grains = 1 KB, OutSwizzleBuf 8x16 grains = 2 KB} = 4 KB; q 2 parts x 8 rows x 128 B = 2 KB; xColMax[2] + xColSum[2][4] = 320 B; gemm0CurrentSeqMax/gemm1AccColMax/Sum 96 B; metaPages 1 KB + metaFormats 256 B; kScales/vScales [4 tiles][64][8 B] = 4 KB; barriers ~30 x 8 B. 2 CTAs/SM cap = 227 KB/2 - 1 KB reserve ≈ 112.5 KB → 1.9 KB headroom.

BARRIERS (all CtaBarrier = custom MBarrier, try_wait.parity/try_wait poll loop, suspend hint 0xFFFFFFFF, no nanosleep):
 kBar[3].produced count 256 = gemm0 128 (self-arrive via arrive_and_wait) + K converters 128; kBar[3].consumed count 160 = gemm0 128 + loader 32 (loader arrive_and_wait; converters wait_parity only).
 vBar[3] identical with gemm1 / V converters / V loader.
 kLoadReady[3]/vLoadReady[3] count 161 = converters 128 (arrive_and_wait) + loader 32 + 1 elected arrive_tx.
 xBar[2].produced count 256 = gemm0 128 arrive + gemm1 128 self-arrive; xBar[2].consumed 256 = gemm0 128 self-arrive (inside storeGemm0AccToShm) + gemm1 128 arrive at tile end (pre-armed once at start).
 gemm0WarpGrpBar (128), gemm1WarpGrpBar (128): mbarrier used as intra-group sync (NamedBarrier class exists in barriers.cuh but is unused here).
 Thread-level arrivals per tile per CTA: 256+160+161+256+160+161+256+256+2x128+2x128 = 2178 (x2 CTAs ≈ 4356 per tile-time per SM).

PER-TILE CONTROL FLOW (steady state, tile t, stage s=t%3, xbuf b=t%2):

 gemm1: vBar[s].produced.arrive_and_wait → xBar[b].produced.arrive_and_wait → rescaleGemm1AccForNewColMax_sync: 3 LDS (accColSum, xColMax, accColMax; NoDup 1 float/lane), gemm1WarpGrpBar.arrive, ballot(accColMax<xColMax), [rare: expf + acc*=scale], gemm1WarpGrpBar.wait, warp 3 only: 4 LDS xColSum + adds + 2 STS (shmAccColMax/Sum), gemm1WarpGrpBar.arrive_and_wait → for idxInstK in 0..3: descX addAddr, 2x (descV addAddr, HGMMA m64n8k16 transA V^T x P), commit, wait_group<0> [4 exposed round trips; comment "@fixme: delay wait to next tile"] → (last tile: finalizeAndWriteOut_sync) → xBar[b].consumed.arrive; vBar[s].consumed.arrive.
 K converter (per warp = page): ldgsts waitGroup<1>; __syncwarp; kLoadReady[s].arrive_and_wait; expandPackedStage (in-place, 1 lane per (token,part), 64 values); fence.proxy.async; kBar[s].produced.arrive; issueKCopies(t+2): kBar[(t+2)%3].consumed.wait_parity(...) then cp.async 16 B chunks + 8 B scales; commitGroup.
 Loader warp: publishPages(readTileMeta) ; kBar[s].consumed.arrive_and_wait ; elected: kFormats[s]=formats, arrive_tx(kLoadReady, A16 bytes), TMA per A16 page part ; fillTileMeta every 16 tiles two ahead ; kLoadReady[s].arrive.

GRID / SCHEDULING: gridDim {1, nbSubSeq, nbKHeads*batch=136}; chooseNbSubSeq (host, wave model with slots = SMs x ctasPerSm = 264) picks n=5 for 64 tiles/seq → 680 CTAs, 13 tiles each (12 for idxSubSeq 4) → 3 rounds on 264 slots (152 slots run 3 CTAs, 112 run 2). Multi-block merge: last CTA per (seq,head) (semaphore atom.inc) merges nbSubSeq partials (2 KB + sum/max each) with 8 math warps. XQA_NB_SUB_SEQ env overrides n. MIXED_KV_TRACE stamps (CTA 0, 8 tiles): slots 0 kwait,1 mma,2 smax,3 xarr (gemm0) | 4 vwait,5 xwait,6 rs,7 mma (gemm1) | 8-11 loaders | 12-15 converters; MIXED_KV_EXPERIMENT bits 1/2/4.

levers.name: L1. Single commit / deferred wgmma wait in gemm1 (remove 3 of 4 exposed PV round trips)
levers.mechanism: In the SWAP_AB bf16 (CACHE_ELEM_ENUM 0/5) gemm1 loop there is no register-resident fragA, so the per-idxInstK commit_group + wait_group<0> is purely conservative. Issue all 8 HGMMA (4 k-steps x 2 m) then one commit; move the wait_group<0> to the top of the next iteration, just before rescaleGemm1AccForNewColMax_sync touches acc (the wait then overlaps vBar/xBar waits), with the tile's xBar.consumed/vBar.consumed arrives issued after that wait (they must stay after the MMAs that read X/V). Last tile: wait before finalize.
levers.analytic_model: gemm1 chain today = 4 x (issue ~40 + wgmma latency L_mma 120-200 cyc). After: 8 issues (~150 cyc) + 1 L_mma overlapped with the next tile's barrier waits. Saves 3 x L_mma + 3 x issue-bubble ≈ 400-600 cycles = 0.2-0.3 us from T_g1.
levers.predicted_effect: If cadence = T_g0 + T_g1 (lock-step hypothesis): 1.5 → ~1.25 us/tile → steady 49.5 → 41 us; total 62 → ~54 us (all q=1 modes' consumer floor). If cadence = max(T_g0,T_g1) with gemm0 binding: 0 wall effect, but gemm1 slack grows (needed anyway before L8). No effect on FP4 production time until the converter chain (2.9 us/tile) is below the consumer cadence.
levers.verification: cuobjdump -sass: WARPGROUP.DEPBAR.LE count in gemm1 region 4 → 1 per tile, HGMMA count unchanged (8); MIXED_KV_TRACE slot7-slot6 shrinks from ~4x(issue+L) to ~issue; ncu: smsp__warps_issue_stalled_wait (wgmma) for gemm1 warps drops.
levers.cost_and_risk: ~15 lines; acc is read by rescale only after the wait; X buffer b and V stage s must not be released before the deferred wait — move the two arrives after it (they currently sit at the end of the same iteration, so moving them one iteration later delays the release by one tile: X ring depth 2 then has 1 free entry for gemm0 → check gemm0 slot3-slot2 does not grow; V stage release one tile later reduces converter lead from 2 to effectively 1.7 tiles — alternatively wait_group<0> at the END of the iteration after the arrives are impossible; so do the wait at the end of the tile (single commit, single wait) as the safe first step: still saves 3 round trips).
levers.depends_on: None. Safe first step: single commit + single wait at tile end (no protocol change).
levers.files_and_functions: csrc/xqa/mha_sm90.cu: gemm1 branch (warpIdx.z==1), the '#pragma unroll for (idxInstK ...)' loop under SWAP_AB / CACHE_ELEM_ENUM 0||5: gmma::commit_group(); gmma::wait_group<0>().

levers.name: L2. Register-resident running colMax/colSum in gemm1 (remove both gemm1WarpGrpBar round trips and the smem exchange)
levers.mechanism: gemm1AccColMax/gemm1AccColSum live in smem and are updated by warp 3 behind two barriers. At N=8 each lane holds exactly one column value (loadShmColWiseVecNoDup: divUp(8,32)=1 float). Keep accColMax/accColSum in registers in every warp; each warp reads xColMax[b] and the 4 xColSum[b][w] slots (already published by gemm0 before xBar.produced.arrive, release/acquire ordered) and updates its own copy identically; write to smem once at the end for finalizeAndWriteOut_sync / multi-block scratch.
levers.analytic_model: Removes 2 mbarrier round trips (RT 150-400 cyc each) + warp-3 LDS/STS chain (~100 cyc) from T_g1: 400-900 cycles = 0.2-0.45 us. Adds 3 LDS per warp (xColSum slots) in parallel, ~30 cyc. Register cost +2 per thread (budget 48, gemm1 acc is 8 floats).
levers.predicted_effect: T_g1 0.65-1.1 → 0.25-0.45 us (with L1). Under lock-step: cadence 1.5 → ~1.05 us → steady 49.5 → 35 us. Under max(): gemm1 is far from binding; effect visible only in trace.
levers.verification: SASS: SYNCS.ARRIVE + SYNCS.PHASECHK sites in gemm1 region drop from 4 to 2 per tile; MIXED_KV_TRACE slot6-slot5 (rescale) collapses from 2 RTs to ~60 cycles; bit-exact test matrix unchanged (same arithmetic order per column).
levers.cost_and_risk: ~40 lines in rescaleGemm1AccForNewColMax_sync/finalize; ballot-based warp-uniform rescale branch stays (all lanes hold the same 8 columns so needRescale is naturally uniform per column pair). Low risk.
levers.files_and_functions: mha_sm90.cu rescaleGemm1AccForNewColMax_sync, finalizeAndWriteOut_sync (SWAP_AB), gemm1 multi-block save of colMax/colSum, SharedMem::gemm1AccColMax/Sum.

levers.name: L3. One barrier per tile for gemm0 colMax (per-warp slots, parity double-buffered, running max in registers)
levers.mechanism: Replace atomicMax into gemm0CurrentSeqMax + 2 arrive_and_wait with: each warp STS its tile-local column max (2 floats, lanes<4) into slot[warp][t%2]; one group sync; every warp LDS the 4 slots, max with its register-resident running max → identical value in all warps. Slot[w][t%2] was last read at tile t-2 and all warps passed the tile t-1 sync between → no WAR hazard, no init, no atomics.
levers.analytic_model: Removes 1 RT (150-400 cyc) + 2 ATOMS round trips (~70 cyc) from T_g0 → 0.1-0.25 us.
levers.predicted_effect: T_g0 0.6-1.1 → 0.5-0.85 us. Lock-step: cadence -0.1..-0.25 us (62 → ~57 alone; cumulative with L1/L2 → ~1.0 us/tile → ~46 us total). Max(): direct if gemm0 binds.
levers.verification: SASS: ATOMS count in gemm0 region 0; SYNCS.ARRIVE per tile in gemm0 4 → 3; trace slot2-slot1 = shuffles (~150 cyc) + 1 RT.
levers.cost_and_risk: ~30 lines; running max also needed by mask path (safeInitRowMax). Low risk.
levers.files_and_functions: mha_sm90.cu computeWarpGrpColMax_sync, SharedMem::gemm0CurrentSeqMax → per-warp slots [2][4][8].

levers.name: L4. Defer colSum reduction to the epilogue (drop 3 SHFL rounds + xColSum STS per tile) and the dead kE4M3_MAX scaling
levers.mechanism: Each thread keeps a per-column partial sum of P over the tokens it owns (2 floats), rescaled by exp(oldMax-newMax) whenever its columns' max changes (same factor gemm1 applies to acc); reduce across lanes (3 SHFL rounds) and warps (smem) once in finalize. gemm1 no longer needs xColSum. Also remove acc*=kE4M3_MAX / xScale pair on the bf16 P path (exact no-op pair only up to rounding — check bit-exactness; P is rounded to bf16 after the multiply, so removing both changes rounding: keep unless test passes).
levers.analytic_model: Per tile: -6 SHFL (~75 cyc dependent) -6 FADD -1 STS -4 FMUL; ~0.04-0.06 us on T_g0. Epilogue +1 reduction per CTA (negligible).
levers.predicted_effect: T_g0 -0.05 us; cadence -0.05 (lock-step). Small but free, and prerequisite for the fused consumer (L8) where per-thread sums are natural.
levers.verification: SASS SHFL.BFLY count in gemm0 per tile 12 → 6; STS to xColSum gone; bit-exact matrix (sum order changes → if not bit-exact vs A16-through-same-kernel, both paths change identically so the test still passes).
levers.cost_and_risk: ~30 lines; requires L3's register-resident running max to know when to rescale the partial sums.
levers.files_and_functions: computeWarpColSum, storeGemm0AccToShm caller, finalizeAndWriteOut_sync, SharedMem::xColSum.

levers.name: L5. Hardware named barriers for the intra-warp-group syncs (gemm0WarpGrpBar, gemm1WarpGrpBar)
levers.mechanism: The two intra-group syncs are mbarriers (128 thread arrivals + try_wait poll loop each). Replace with NamedBarrier (bar.sync id,128) from barriers.cuh (ids 3/4; ids 1/2 were reserved for the converters' hazard barrier, now __syncwarp). A bar.sync parks the warp in the CTA barrier unit: no SYNCS traffic, no spin instructions, ~20-40 cycles after the last arrival.
levers.analytic_model: Per sync: RT_mbarrier (150-400 cyc) → ~40 cyc; today 4 syncs/tile (2 gemm0 + 2 gemm1) → saves 4 x (RT-40) = 440-1440 cyc = 0.22-0.7 us if all four remain; with L2/L3 only 1 sync/tile remains → 0.06-0.18 us. Also removes 512 thread-arrivals and 4 poll loops per tile from the SYNCS unit (helps L6's contention).
levers.predicted_effect: Alone: cadence 1.5 → 1.1-1.3 us (lock-step) → total ~50-55 us; with L2/L3 the residual gain is 0.06-0.18 us/tile. Also lowers issue-active % (spin instr gone) at equal or better cadence.
levers.verification: SASS: BAR.SYNC appears in consumer regions, SYNCS.PHASECHK sites drop; ncu sm__issue_active drops while duration does not rise; PC sampling: no samples on the removed try_wait loops.
levers.cost_and_risk: ~10 lines; bar.sync requires all 128 threads convergent at the call (consumer code is warp-uniform). No cross-role change.

levers.name: L6. Elected-lane aggregated mbarrier arrivals (arrive(update=32) after __syncwarp) for every per-thread arrive in the tile loop
levers.mechanism: kBar/vBar/xBar produced+consumed and kLoadReady/vLoadReady are arrived by all 128 threads (2178 thread-arrivals per tile per CTA, ~4356 per SM tile-time). MBarrier::arrive(update) already emits mbarrier.arrive.release.cta.b64 with a count operand; after __syncwarp() (intra-warp memory ordering), one lane per warp arrives with update=32. Counts stay identical; waits become wait_parity (no self-arrive) where the role only needs to observe (gemm0 on kBar.produced, gemm1 on vBar.produced/xBar.produced, gemm0 on xBar.consumed) — halving the arrival counts (kBar.produced 256→128 etc.). This is CUTLASS PipelineTmaAsync's pattern (one arrival per warp/warpgroup).
levers.analytic_model: Hypothesis to test first: the converter level-3 trace shows 'proxy fence + produced arrive = 0.45 us' (~900 cyc) for 128 thread-arrivals, i.e. ~7 cyc per lane arrival if serialized in the SYNCS path. If arrivals serialize at c cycles/lane, each 128-thread arrive costs 32c per warp (on the arriving warp's chain) and 128c of SYNCS occupancy; the consumers perform 8 warp-level arrives per role per tile → 8 x 31c ≈ 250c cycles saved per role chain (c=2: 0.25 us; c=7: 0.9 us — the latter exceeds the chain, so c is probably ≤3 for the consumer path; the 0.45 us may be dominated by the fence). Upper bound on total-arrival load: 4356 → ~140 per SM tile-time.
levers.predicted_effect: Conditional: if the converter segment drops from 0.45 us to <0.1 us with elected arrival, expect T_g0 and T_g1 to each shrink 0.1-0.3 us and the converter cadence 2.9 → ~2.5 us/tile (FP4 96 → ~85 us) — the only lever here that also moves the production FP4 number today. If the segment does not move, the fence dominates and L6 is a no-op: reject after one measurement.
levers.verification: Step 1 (cheap): change only the converters' kBar/vBar.produced.arrive to elected update=32 and read level-3 trace 'fenced+produced' segment (slot 8 - slot 13). Step 2: apply to consumers; ncu PC sampling stall on SYNCS.ARRIVE lines; l1tex shared-memory atomic/SYNCS pipe utilization metric.
levers.cost_and_risk: ~20 sites; correctness relies on __syncwarp before the elected arrive for other lanes' smem writes (stmatrix X, expansion writes) — same reasoning CUTLASS uses (fence + elected arrive). The release ordering of the elected lane covers writes that happen-before via __syncwarp. Medium risk of subtle ordering bugs; bounded test matrix catches them (hang or mismatch).

levers.name: L7. Software-pipeline gemm0: issue tile t+1's QK^T HGMMAs before softmax(t) (double-buffered 4-float accumulator)
levers.mechanism: gemm0 waits kBar[t+1].produced (normally already complete: converters run 2 ahead) and issues the next tile's 8 HGMMA into acc[(t+1)%2] right after wait_group for tile t; then does softmax(t) on acc[t%2] while the tensor pipe works. At the loop top: wait_group<0> (now already retired) instead of a cold issue+wait.
levers.analytic_model: Hides L_mma + issue ≈ 200-300 cycles per tile behind softmax (0.1-0.15 us). Cost: acc x2 = +4 regs; kBar.consumed arrive for stage t+1 moves after its MMAs complete (still one tile later than today's release → converter lead unchanged since release happens right after wait at the next loop top).
levers.predicted_effect: T_g0 -0.1..-0.15 us; with L3/L4/L5: T_g0 ≈ 0.35-0.5 us. Cumulative L1-L7: T_g0 ≈ 0.35-0.5, T_g1 ≈ 0.25-0.4 → cadence 0.6-0.9 (sum) / 0.35-0.5 (max) → steady-state 20-30 us / 12-16 us; total with today's fixed ≈ 32-42 / 24-29 us — at or below the FP4 target (36) on the consumer side.
levers.verification: Trace slot1-slot0 collapses to the wait cost (~50 cyc) except on tiles where K arrives late (then it measures converter lag, which is the right thing to see); SASS shows HGMMA issue before the softmax block in program order.
levers.cost_and_risk: ~30 lines; the K stage for t+1 must exist (nbKBuf=3 ≥ 2 in flight: fine). Loop peeling for the first/last tile.

levers.name: L8. Fused consumer warp groups (FA3 pattern): each of the two 4-warp groups does QK^T → softmax → PV for alternate tiles; the X ring, xColMax/xColSum exchange and gemm1 rescale barriers disappear
levers.mechanism: gemm0 and gemm1 are split across warp groups only because upstream XQA wanted a 2-stage GEMM pipeline; at N=8 the accumulators are 4 + 8 floats, so one group can hold both. New consumer loop per group g∈{0,1}, tiles t ≡ g (mod 2): kBar[s].produced wait → 8 HGMMA QK → wait → scale/mask → per-warp local max → 1 bar.sync exchange (L3) → exp2, per-thread partial sums (L4) → bf16 P → STSM into the group's private P buffer [t%2] (1 KB; 2 groups x 2 = 4 KB = today's X union) → bar.sync + fence.proxy.async (same-group producer/consumer of smem for wgmma) → vBar[s].produced wait → 8 HGMMA PV (P as B operand from smem, V^T transA) → single commit, wait deferred to next tile's rescale → kBar/vBar consumed arrive (elected). Rescale of the O accumulator is register-local (each thread's acc columns = its 2 heads = the columns whose running max it holds). Merge the two groups' (O, max, sum) at the end with the existing multi-block combine arithmetic (in-CTA, via the OutSwizzleBuf/scratch path). K/V stage ownership alternates by tile parity; barrier counts are unchanged (both groups are 128 threads); converter/loader roles untouched.
levers.analytic_model: Per-tile chain per group ≈ kBar wait 100 + QK issue+latency 250 (or overlapped, L7) + max 100 + bar.sync 60 + exp/cvt 60 + STSM+bar.sync+fence 100 + vBar wait 100 + PV issue 150 (wait deferred) ≈ 900 cyc ≈ 0.45 us; two groups interleave → CTA cadence ≈ 0.23-0.3 us/tile (bounded below by smem read for HGMMA 256 cyc/CTA-tile = 0.13 us and by the 2-CTA smem budget 0.33 us/tile-time for FP4 at 81 KB per CTA-tile). Instruction count per tile per CTA ≈ 500-600 warp-instr (from ~1200 + 900 spin). Barrier RTs per tile per group: 2 mbarrier (kBar, vBar) + 2 bar.sync. Registers: 4 + 8 acc + 2 P words + 2 max + 2 sum + descriptors ~16 + loop/state ~10 ≈ 44-48; pool allows 52 per consumer group (128x24 + 256x56 + 256x52 = 30720).
levers.predicted_effect: Consumer floor per tile per CTA 1.5 → ~0.25-0.3 us → steady-state consumer time 8704 x 0.28 / 264 ≈ 9 us; the consumer stops being the floor for every mode. The kernel floor becomes max(DRAM: A16 59 / FP8 32 / FP4 17 / mixed 36 us; smem BW ≈ 21 us for FP4 expansion; converter chain 2.9 us/tile today → must drop below ~0.6 us/tile (5x) to reach 36 us FP4 — that is the converter-side item, not this one). Predicted wall clock after L8 alone: FP4 still ≈ 90 us (converter-paced); A16 83 (DRAM); i.e. L8 is necessary, not sufficient — verify by trace/SASS, not stopwatch.
levers.verification: cuobjdump: consumer region instruction count per tile ≈ halves; HGMMA count per tile 16 unchanged; SYNCS.PHASECHK sites in consumer loop = 2; BAR.SYNC = 2; STSM = 1; FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC = 1. Trace: new per-group stamps (kwait, qk done, smax done, P stored, vwait, pv issued) show ≈ 900 cyc per tile per group. ncu: issue-active from consumer warps ≈ 10%; PC-sampling spin share on consumer warps → converter waits only. Bit-exact matrix incl. SPEC_DEC off (q=1) and >1 work item per CTA.
levers.cost_and_risk: Largest change (~300-400 lines, new loop assembled from existing pieces: gemm0 HGMMA loop, softmax helpers, storeGemm0AccToShm, gemm1 HGMMA loop, rescale, finalize/merge). Risks: register cap 52 (spills visible as STACK>0 / LDL); ordering of same-group STSM → wgmma read needs bar.sync + fence.proxy.async (FA3 keeps P in registers so has no exact analogue; CUTLASS epilogue smem→TMA uses fence_view_async_shared + NamedBarrier); the tile-parity split halves each group's sequential tile count so per-group max/sum diverge — merge math already exists (multi-block combine). Alternating groups also require the converters to produce tiles in order (they do).
levers.depends_on: L1-L5, L7 are stepping stones (their code becomes the fused loop); L6 independent. Persistent scheduling (L9) is orthogonal.
levers.files_and_functions: mha_sm90.cu: warpIdx.z==0 and ==1 branches (replace with one consumer body parameterized by group), SharedMem::reusedXVOutSwizzleBuf/xColMax/xColSum (→ 2x2 P buffers), xBar (remove), kBar/vBar init counts (gemm 128 + converters/loader unchanged), finalizeAndWriteOut_sync + multi-block combine (in-CTA merge of two groups). Reference: include/flashinfer/attention/hopper/mainloop_mma.cuh (consumer_wait K → gemm QK (wg_wait -1) → rescale_o → consumer_wait V → gemm PV → warpgroup_wait<1> → release K → softmax update → warpgroup_wait<0> → release V).

levers.name: L9. Persistent / balanced CTA scheduling (kill wave quantization and per-CTA fill)
levers.mechanism: Today chooseNbSubSeq picks n=5 → 680 uniform CTAs on 264 slots = 3 rounds x 13 tiles (39 tile-times) + 3 fills per slot. Replace with a persistent grid of exactly slots=264 CTAs pulling (seq-head, tile range) items from a global atomic counter with ranges sized so each CTA processes ≈ 33 tiles (a CTA may finish one sub-sequence and start another: finalize → partial write → next item, reusing the existing multi-block scratch/merge). Prefetch the next item's metadata (fillTileMeta) and first copies during the current item's last tiles so the fill (2 dependent DRAM loads + first landing) is paid once per slot, not per item.
levers.analytic_model: Steady tile-times 39 → 33 (-15%); fills per slot 3 → 1 (-2f, f ≈ 1-3 us); merge count unchanged in total. Total ≈ 33 x T_tile + f + merge. At T_tile=1.5: 49.5 + ~2 + ~1 ≈ 53 us (from 62). At T_tile=0.7 (after L1-L7): 23 + 3 ≈ 26 us; at 0.28 (L8): 9 + 3 ≈ 12 us. Calibrate the wave model first with XQA_NB_SUB_SEQ=3 (predicted 2x22=44 tile-times vs n=5's 39 → duration ratio ≈ 1.13) — no code change.
levers.predicted_effect: -9 us at today's cadence (62 → ~53), and the same absolute saving persists after the cadence levers, where it becomes the dominant term (26 → 17 would need it).
levers.verification: Per-CTA %globaltimer start/end stamps (extend the trace to all CTAs, 2 words each) → histogram of slot idle time and tail; ncu sm__cycles_active.max vs .avg (imbalance); launch stats show 264 CTAs; kernel duration vs predicted 33 x T_tile + f.
levers.cost_and_risk: Medium: work-item loop around the existing per-CTA body (all roles re-enter their tile loops; barrier phases/parities continue across items — kBar/vBar/xBar parity words become per-CTA running counters, cf. FA3 amendment A5's cross-item K(last) hazard), scratch sized for the item count, semaphore per (seq,head) unchanged. Alternative cheap variant: choose n and slots so that CTAs = k x 264 with balanced tile counts (not possible for 136 seq-heads: 264/136 not rational-friendly) → persistence is the only exact fix.
levers.depends_on: Independent of L1-L8; do after the RT calibration (L5) because its payoff is measured in tile-times.
levers.files_and_functions: mha_sm90.cu chooseNbSubSeq (host), kernel_mha grid/indices (idxReq/idxHeadGrp/idxSubSeq from blockIdx → from a work counter), fillTileMeta/prefetch across items, ScratchMem sizing, launchHopperF8MHAFlashInfer grid.

levers.name: L10. Bigger KV tile per softmax step (128 tokens) — analyzed and rejected under the 2-CTA/SM smem budget
levers.mechanism: Doubling gemm0CtaTileNbTokens to 128 halves the number of skeleton executions per token; acc 8 floats, 16+16 HGMMA per tile, X entry 2 KB. But K/V stages become 32 KB: K3V3 = 192 KB or K2V2 = 128 KB → 1 CTA/SM (slots 132). Variant 'consume two 64-token stages per softmax step' needs K4V4 (128 KB) for one-step-ahead buffering → same occupancy loss.
levers.analytic_model: T_tile(128) ≈ T_tile(64) x 1.15-1.3 (MMA latency/issue doubles, everything else constant) ≈ 1.75-1.95 us; tiles 4352 over 132 slots → 58-64 us steady vs 49.5 today. Even after L1-L7 (T64 ≈ 0.7 → T128 ≈ 0.85): 4352 x 0.85/132 = 28 us vs 8704 x 0.7/264 = 23 us. Always loses to keeping 2 CTAs/SM; L8 gets the 'two tiles per skeleton' effect (two groups) without changing stage size.
levers.predicted_effect: Negative (+10-30% on the consumer floor). Do not pursue.
levers.verification: None needed beyond the smem arithmetic: sizeof(SharedMem) with gemm0CtaTileNbTokens=128 ≥ 160 KB → cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor = 1.

levers.name: L11. 3 CTAs/SM — analyzed: infeasible with the 5-warp-group CTA, dominated by L8
levers.mechanism: Occupancy 3 needs ≤ 74.6 KB smem (227/3 - 1 KB reserve) and ≤ 34 regs/thread at 640 threads (65536/1920). Smem: K2V2 (-32 KB) + scale ring 4→3 (-1 KB) + meta 2→1 chunk (-0.6 KB) → ~77 KB, still over; and K2 puts the copies only 1 tile ahead (landing 1.9 us > cadence — measured worse in backends.md item 1). Registers: 34/thread is below what the converters (56) and gemm groups (48) use; a 3-WG CTA (384 threads → 56 regs) would have to merge loader+K+V converters into one group (half the conversion lanes per CTA: 8→4 warps).
levers.analytic_model: If it were feasible at T_tile unchanged: 8704 x 1.5 / 396 = 33 us steady. But it forces K2V2 (converter chain +0.9 us/tile measured) and 12 vs 16 converter warps per SM. Net negative for compressed streams; irrelevant for A16 (DRAM-bound).
levers.predicted_effect: Not a floor lever in practice. L8 delivers 2 consumer pipelines per CTA inside the current 110.6 KB / 48-reg footprint.
levers.verification: n/a; smem/register arithmetic above.
levers.cost_and_risk: n/a (rejected).

Costs +2 KB → 112.6 KB > 112.5 cap; recover 1 KB by nbScaleTiles 4 → 3 (copies are issued 2 ahead after tile t's expansion completes, so live scale entries are t+1, t+2 and the one being issued: 3 suffice) → 111.6 KB, 2 CTAs/SM preserved.

levers.predicted_effect: 0 or up to -0.4 us/tile (62 → ~50 us). Superseded by L8 (no ring).
levers.verification: Trace slot3-slot2 and slot5-slot4 before/after; MIXED_KV_XDEPTH=3 build with nbScaleTiles=3; occupancy API still returns 2.

K converter warp w: prologue wait kPagesReady; issue copies for t=0,1 (kAhead=2: consumed.wait_parity(stage) then issueCompressedPageCopies = cp.async 16 B chunks, lane owns chunk (lane%8 / lane%4) of rows, swizzle-encoded dest into the stage's LAST part buffer, + 8 B scales, ~30 instr/lane) + commitGroup; loop: waitGroup<1> -> syncwarp -> kLoadReady.arrive_and_wait -> expandPackedStage (lane = (token, part): read scale word + 4x16B (FP8) or 2x16B (FP4) packed chunks from the last part buffer, syncwarp, convertE4M3x4ScalesToA16Bits, per block: cvt e4m3x2->f16x2->bf16x2 (FP8) or cutlass _e2m1_to_bf16_x8 LUT (FP4), mul bf16x2, two 16 B stores per block; A16 lanes return after the syncwarp) -> fence.proxy.async -> kBar.produced.arrive -> issue copies for t+2 -> commitGroup. gemm0: produced.arrive_and_wait once per stage -> 16 wgmma (both parts) -> commit -> wait_group<0> -> consumed.arrive -> same softmax/handoff as stock. gemm1: vBar.produced.arrive_and_wait (plain) -> otherwise identical to stock (still 4 serial wait_group<0>). Hops on the A16 path: TMA tx -> kLoadReady -> converter (syncwarp, fence, arrive) -> kBar.produced -> gemm0 (one extra warp wake-up vs stock). wgmma operand facts (gmma_impl.cuh): SS form `mma_async_shmA<T,n,transA,transB>` for all combos; RS form `mma_async_regA` generated ONLY for transA==0 (A = 4 x b32 per thread = the 64x16 A tile; B always a smem descriptor). In SWAP_AB gemm0 A=K (transA=0) and gemm1 A=V (transA=1, i.e. V^T from token-major rows) -> K could be RS directly, V only after a register-side transpose (as the fp8-cache path does with ldmatrix.trans in loadVTileTransposed). Dead code: loadMixedKTileFragment / loadMixedVTileFragment (RS fragment decoders, lines 614-847) are defined but never called.

levers.name: L1 Shorten the consumer dependent chain (topology-independent; the only route to the FP8/mixed targets and a prerequisite for FP4)
levers.mechanism: (a) gemm1: hoist `gmma::wait_group<0>()` out of the idxInstK loop (one commit per k-step, one wait after the 4th; descV/descX are smem descriptors so no register lifetime issue) -> 3 fewer wgmma drains per tile. (b) gemm0 colMax: double-buffer smem.gemm0CurrentSeqMax by tile parity so the second gemm0WarpGrpBar.arrive_and_wait (which only protects the next tile's atomicMax from slow readers) is removed; or reduce with one shfl-tree per warp + one smem exchange + one sync. (c) storeGemm0AccToShm: split xBar.consumed.arrive_and_wait into arrive at loop top (right after the previous tile's stmatrix) and wait immediately before stmatrix, so gemm1's release latency overlaps the whole softmax. (d) Replace the two intra-warpgroup mbarrier syncs per group per tile with hardware named barriers (NamedBarrier in barriers.cuh, `bar.sync id,128`; ids 1/2 are now free since expandPackedStage uses __syncwarp), removing 2 x 128 arrives + poll loops per tile per group. (e) Converters: fence.proxy.async + produced.arrive measured at 0.45 us -> issue the fence per warp right after its own stores and arrive with count 32 from one lane (the produced count is 256 = 128 gemm0 + 128 converter; change to 128 + 4 and arrive(32)... or keep the count and let the lane arrive with update=32).
levers.analytic_model: Chain model: T_CTA_tile = sum over dependent steps of (step latency at w warps/scheduler). Anchor: 1.88 us per CTA-tile at w=10 (62 us floor). Each removed dependent step (wgmma drain ~100-150 cyc, mbarrier warpgroup sync ~150-300 cyc incl. wake-up, consumed wait ~100-300) saves its own latency; (a)+(b)+(c)+(d) remove ~7 steps from the longer of the two group chains -> 0.35-0.9 us of 1.88 us.
levers.predicted_effect: Floor 62 us -> 45-55 us (P_SM 0.68-0.83 us). With converters hidden (L2/L3): FP8 -> 48-58 us (target 58), mixed -> 50-60 us (target 62), FP4 -> 46-56 us (target 36 still not met). A16 unchanged (DRAM-bound).

(d) requires all 4 warps of a group to reach the bar.sync (they do; the group is convergent per tile).

levers.name: L2 Minimal topology for mixed pages on sm90: 4 warp groups (gemm0, gemm1, K-converter+loader, V-converter+loader)
levers.mechanism: Delete the IO group. Converter warp w already owns page w's compressed copies; give it page w's A16 TMA boxes too (elected lane issues 2 boxes on kLoadReady when it issues the tile's cp.async copies, 2 tiles ahead), so the 8 boxes per operand are spread over 4 warps (0.23 us each instead of 1 us serialized in one lane). Q load (once) and the metadata chunk fills move to converter warp 0 (K) / warp 0 (V) before their loops; the loader's per-tile consumed.arrive_and_wait/publishPages/kFormats store/kLoadReady.arrive collapse into the converter's existing consumed.wait_parity and kLoadReady.arrive_and_wait (kLoadReady count 161 -> 129: 128 converters + 1 tx-arrive per warp... use 4 tx-arrives, count 132). Launch bounds (512, 2) -> 64 regs/thread; setmaxnreg gemm 48 / converters 80 (pool 2*128*48 + 2*128*80 = 32768 = 512*64). Smem unchanged (~108 KB, 2 CTAs/SM). Warps/SM 40 -> 32 (10 -> 8 per scheduler); two idle IO warps and two polling loader warps disappear.
levers.analytic_model: Fair-share hypothesis (consumer chain paced by issue share, cycles/instr ~ 1.33 x warps/scheduler, anchored at 13.3 @ 10): L_chain(8) = 1.88 x 8/10 = 1.50 us -> P_SM 0.75 us -> 50 us floor. Latency-bound hypothesis (chain fixed by barrier/wgmma latencies): ~62 us unchanged. Converter budget per operand: expansion ~1.6 us + copy issue 0.64 + TMA issue 0.23 (A16 pages) + fence/arrive 0.45 = ~2.9 us per tile in 4 warps, i.e. STILL the pacer unless L1(e) and more converter lanes (T3 has no idle lanes to add) -> expansion must be cut by 2x: 8 converter lanes per token instead of 4 is impossible at 4 WGs, so the converter pacing (2.9 us) vs consumer (1.5-1.9 us) gap must close via (i) L1(e) fence/arrive (0.45 -> ~0.1), (ii) copy issue already lean, (iii) expansion 1.6 us for 230 instr/lane = 13.8 cyc/instr -> at 8 warps/scheduler ~11 -> 1.3 us. Predicted converter cadence ~2.0 us.
levers.predicted_effect: FP8/FP4/mixed cadence min(converter ~2.0, consumer 1.5-1.9) -> ~2.0 us per CTA-tile -> ~66 us (+tail) at 2 CTAs/SM, from 91/96/114 today; with L1 applied the consumer drops to 1.2-1.5 and the converter (2.0) paces -> FP8 ~60-66, FP4 ~62-66, mixed ~66-70. Register headroom (64) also removes the SPEC_DEC-style cap for N=16 (q<=4) consumers if mha_sm90 is later enabled for spec-dec. Bounded payoff ~20-30%, matching the record's estimate; does not reach FP4 36.

Risk that the consumer is latency-bound (then L2 alone yields ~0).

levers.name: L3 Negative result to record: 3-WG stock kernel with in-register (RS-wgmma) conversion is quantitatively worse on sm90
levers.mechanism: SWAP_AB already makes K and V the A operand (that is the layout trick: q=1 puts the 8 Q heads in N). RS wgmma (mma_async_regA, A = 4 x b32 per thread, B smem descriptor) exists but only for transA=0, so K (gemm0) can be fed from registers directly while V (gemm1, transA=1) needs a register-side transpose: the fragment loader gathers 4 single bytes/nibbles from 4 different token rows per pair (as the dead loadMixedVTileFragment does). Warp w's A rows 16w..16w+15 are exactly page w, so the per-page format branch is warp-uniform.
levers.analytic_model: Per k-step per thread (8 values): K FP8 ~35 instr (4 x 16-bit LDS, 4 cvt.e4m3x2, f16->bf16 4 x 3, 2 scale cvt, 4 bf16x2 mul), K FP4 ~40, V (transposed gathers) ~40-50. Per tile: gemm0 8 k-steps + gemm1 8 fragments -> 600-700 instr/thread = 4800-5600 warp-instr per CTA-tile ON the consumer chain (vs 1840 [230 x 8 warps] off-chain today). Per-value decode 2.5-3 instr (no x8 LUT, byte gathers) vs 0.9-1.4 row-wise. The m64n8k16 wgmma finishes in ~10-20 cycles per k-step; decode per k-step is 35-50 instr = 3-4x the MMA it feeds, so it cannot hide behind the async MMA. At even 4 cycles/instr (uncontended), +2400-2800 cycles = +1.2-1.4 us per group per tile on a 1.0-1.9 us chain.

No target met; worse than or equal to the current 5-WG build. Confirms the backends.md rejection with numbers.

(b) Move the Q load off the K-loader warp onto an idle IO warp (warps 2/3) so the first K TMA is not behind the Q round trip. (c) Replace the wave-quantized grid (680 CTAs / 264 slots = 2.58 waves) with a persistent grid of exactly 132 x ctasPerSm CTAs pulling (req, head, chunk) work items from an atomic counter, or choose nbSubSeq to make 136 x n close to a multiple of 264 while keeping the merge cost (cost model exists in chooseNbSubSeq).

Total 8-10 us out of 62-96 us in consumer-bound modes (FP4/FP8/mixed); A16 (DRAM-bound) loses less because the other CTA's traffic fills the bandwidth.

levers.name: L5 Enable PDL for the mixed build

levers.name: L1: Diagnose the converter's own issue rate (prerequisite artifact, not a code change)
levers.mechanism: The converter warp issues one instruction per ~11-14 cycles in BOTH the ALU-dominated expansion (310 instr / 3350 cycles) and the LSU/address-dominated copy issue (~40 instr / 1270 cycles), while the scheduler is idle 42% of the time with only ~1.7 eligible warps. A warp that is eligible would issue every ~1.7 cycles; therefore the converter warp is mostly NOT eligible, i.e. stalled on its own dependencies, not starved by spinners. Candidates, in order: (a) MIO/LSU back-pressure on STS.128/LDGSTS (16 warps per SM each pushing 8 x 512 B bursts in phase with wgmma's 16 KB descriptor reads) -> stall_mio_throttle / lg_throttle / short_scoreboard at STS/LDS PCs; (b) fixed-latency dependency chains at ILP~1 because the 4-block loop is not interleaved under the 56-register cap and the asm volatile conversions -> stall_wait; (c) instruction-cache misses from 5 role bodies (~12K SASS instr) sharing the SM -> stall_no_instruction; (d) not_selected against the other CTA's converter warps on the same scheduler.
levers.analytic_model: 3350 cycles / 310 instr = 10.8 cycles per instruction; an uncontended issue would be 1-3 cycles per instruction (4-6 cycle ALU latency / ILP 2-4), so 8-9 cycles per instruction are stall; which stall class holds them decides whether the rate levers (L4/L5/L7) or the count levers (L2/L3/L6) pay off. The record's stall mix is kernel-wide and dominated by the try_wait spinners (long_sb on the TRYWAIT result), so it says nothing about converter PCs.
levers.predicted_effect: No timing change by itself; it partitions the 1.69 us: if (a) dominates, L5 (deferred fence / store-drain overlap) and RS-K (L7) are the levers; if (b), L4 (64 regs, drop asm volatile, hoist lane-constant addresses) can recover up to ~2x on the expansion (1.69 -> ~0.9 us); if (c), code-size reduction (static-format builds already remove one decode arm; remove the dead RS fragment loaders :616-830 and dead cp.async helpers from the sm90 TU); if (d), nothing converter-side helps and only fewer instructions do.
levers.verification: ncu --set full with PC sampling (source view) filtered to the PC range of expandPackedStage (identify by the PRMT-dense region between the kLoadReady TRYWAIT loop and FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC): per-PC stall reasons; plus cuobjdump -sass count of the converter body (expect ~310 fp4 / ~245 fp8 SASS instr per lane-tile; 96 PRMT, 32 HMUL2, 8 STS.128 for fp4; 64 HADD2.F32 + 32 F2FP.BF16 for fp8-bf16). This is the missing measured record; everything below quotes its prediction conditional on it.
levers.cost_and_risk: One profiling run on nkcut2; zero code risk.
levers.files_and_functions: csrc/xqa/mha_sm90.cu expandPackedStage (:2734), issueCompressedPageCopies (:2538); cuobjdump on the JIT .cubin

levers.name: L2: Remove the per-tile kLoadReady rendezvous (converters own the stage handshake)
levers.mechanism: Converters already read the tile's tags and page ids from the metadata chunk two tiles earlier (issueCompressedPageCopies); expandPackedStage re-reads the tag from kFormats[s], which the loader publishes under kLoadReady. Keep the warp's tag for tiles t..t+2 in three rotating registers (one byte per warp per tile), so expansion never waits on the loader. For static compressed builds (MIXED_PAGE_STATIC_FORMAT>=1) there is no A16 TMA at all and kLoadReady/vLoadReady vanish at compile time. For mixed streams, retarget the A16 TMA transaction bytes to kBar[s].produced (make produced a tx barrier: loader arrive_tx + 32 arrives, converters 128, gemm0 128) so gemm0's single wait covers both TMA landing and expansion; A16 rows and expanded rows are disjoint so no ordering between loader TMA and converter STS is needed.
levers.analytic_model: Removes the 0.17 us segment (SYNCS.ARRIVE + TRYWAIT round trip + LDS) from a 3.0 us converter-paced period: 3.0 -> 2.83 us; also removes 5 SASS instructions and one poll loop per lane-tile, and one 161-count barrier per stage.
levers.predicted_effect: fp4 96 -> ~91 us, fp8 91 -> ~86, mixed 114 -> ~108 (all still converter-paced); no effect once the converter period is below 1.94 us.
levers.verification: TRACE slot 12-11 -> ~0; cuobjdump: no SYNCS.ARRIVE on kLoadReady in the converter body, kBar produced init shows arrive_tx use (SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64 in the loader), kLoadReady absent from SharedMem for static builds (sizeof(SharedMem) drops by 6 x 8 B).
levers.cost_and_risk: Small protocol change; C7-style deadlock class must be re-read: gemm0 waits produced(t) which now also needs the loader's arrive_tx -> loader must issue before converters can complete, it already does (it waits only on consumed). Bit-exact matrix unchanged.
levers.files_and_functions: mha_sm90.cu :1190-1199 (barrier init), :1857-1891 (K loader), :2104-2113 / :2153-2162 (converters), expandPackedStage formats argument

levers.name: L3: Software-pipeline the store drain: defer fence+produced.arrive(t) until after tile t+1's loads and scale conversion; issue copies(t+3) before the fence
levers.mechanism: Reorder the converter loop body to: wait landed(t+1) -> LDS packed rows + scale word of t+1 (into registers) -> issueCopies(t+3) (dependent LDS/IMAD/LDGSTS chain) -> fence.proxy.async + produced.arrive(t) -> decode/STS of t+1. The 16 KB of STS.128 from tile t drains while the warp does t+1's loads and the copy-issue chain instead of while it sits in the fence; the arrive for t is delayed by ~0.3 us, which is free because gemm0 has 1 us of slack per tile (1.94 vs 3.0) and K depth 3 keeps produced(t) ahead of gemm0's need. Stages t and t+1 are different buffers (no in-place hazard across tiles; the intra-tile __syncwarp stays).
levers.analytic_model: The fence+arrive segment (0.45 us) is a drain wait, and the copy-issue segment (0.64 us) is a latency chain; running them concurrently turns a serial sum 0.45+0.64 into ~max(0.45, 0.64) plus the fence's residual: period 3.0 -> ~2.55 us (with L2: ~2.4). Register cost: the t+1 packed words (fp8: 4 x LdGrain = 16 regs, fp4: 8) and scale word live across the fence -- fits in 56 only for fp4/mixed if the decode temporaries are not simultaneously live; fp8 needs the 64-reg layout (L4) or holding only 2 of the 4 LDS.128 early.
levers.predicted_effect: fp4 96 -> ~80 us (2.4 us cadence with L2), fp8 91 -> ~78, mixed 114 -> ~96 (mixed has fewer compressed pages per tile so its converter period is shorter but its A16 TMA path stays). Still above the consumer floor of 62.
levers.verification: TRACE: segment 13->8 (fence+arrive) collapses to <0.05 us and 8->9 (copy issue) overlaps; SASS shows FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC after the LDGSTS group and after the next tile's LDS.128s; instruction count unchanged (+/- 5).
levers.cost_and_risk: Moderate: loop restructuring with the barrier protocol (produced(t) after landed(t+1) wait: landed(t+1) depends only on the converter's own cp.async groups, never on gemm0, so no cycle). Verify with the timeout-bounded conformance matrix incl. nbIters < 3 tails.
levers.depends_on: L2 recommended first (removes one wait from the reordered body); fp8 variant depends on L4 for registers
levers.files_and_functions: mha_sm90.cu converter loops :2082-2124 and :2131-2166; split expandPackedStage into loadPacked()/decodeStore() halves

levers.name: L4: Four-warp-group layout (loader merged into converters), 64 registers uniform, no setmaxnreg
levers.mechanism: Groups: gemm0, gemm1, K-side (4 warps: converters that also issue the A16 TMA for their own page with an elected lane, Q load by warp 0 once), V-side. 512 threads -> 65536/1024 = 64 regs each at 2 CTAs/SM; kBar.consumed count drops to 128 (no loader), kLoadReady/kPagesReady/pageFormats/pages disappear, two spinning loader warps and two idle warps per CTA are gone (8 fewer warps per SM -> 8 per scheduler). Converter code gets 56 -> 64 regs (room to interleave two blocks' decode chains and to hold L3's early loads); GEMM groups get 48 -> 64 (their skeleton currently lives at the launch-bound 48, unverified whether it serialises).
levers.analytic_model: Subsumes L2 (-0.17 us). If L1 shows stall_wait/ILP-bound expansion, +8 regs lets ptxas overlap the 2 x8 LUT chains of block b with the HMUL2/STS of block b-1: dependent-latency-bound time ~ (chain depth x latency) / ILP; going from ILP~1 to ~2 halves the ALU-bound part (up to -0.8 us of 1.69). If L1 shows MIO-bound, no gain beyond L2. Also gives the SPEC_DEC variant a 64-reg budget instead of 48 (its static demand is 226, so it still spills: SPEC_DEC needs 1 CTA/SM or a q-tiled consumer, separate item).
levers.predicted_effect: fp4 period 3.0 -> 2.2-2.6 us (77-83 us) depending on L1's verdict; combined with L3: ~2.0-2.2 us -> 65-70 us, at the consumer floor for fp8 (62-64 us).
levers.verification: cuobjdump -res-usage REG:64 STACK:0, no USETMAXREG; SASS of the converter body shows interleaved PRMT/HMUL2/STS across blocks (instruction order); ncu launch stats: 16 warps/CTA, 2 CTAs/SM, theoretical occupancy 32 warps; TRACE per-tile converter period.
levers.cost_and_risk: Large restructuring of the IO role (Q load, TMA issue, fillTileMeta move into the converter groups); the A16 TMA per page must be issued by the warp that owns the page after consumed(t) -- same wait it already does in issueKCopies. Keeps the consumer (C5) untouched.
levers.depends_on: L1 verdict decides the payoff; L2/L3 fold into it

levers.name: L5: Reduce FP8->BF16 decode from 5 to 3 instructions per pair (if a packed f16x2->bf16x2 cvt exists on sm90) and hoist lane-constant addressing
levers.mechanism: convertE4M3x2ToA16<bf16> is cvt.rn.f16x2.e4m3x2 -> __half22float2 (2 HADD2.F32) -> __float22bfloat162_rn (F2FP.BF16.PACK) -> mul.rn.bf16x2 = 5 SASS per pair (32 pairs = 160 of the 245 per lane-tile). A direct integer E4M3->BF16 (PRMT spread + SHF + 2 LOP3, exact incl. subnormals when the 2^-120 factor is folded into the block scale, but 448 x 2^120 overflows bf16 so the fold is not free) is also 4+1 = 5, no gain. The only 3-instruction form is F2FP(e4m3x2->f16x2) -> single packed f16x2->bf16x2 convert -> HMUL2, which requires ptxas to accept cvt.rn.bf16x2.f16x2 (or cvt.rn.bf16.f16 x2 = 4) for sm_90 -- to be checked with ptxas, not assumed. Independently: the 8 store chunk offsets (2b+g)^(token%8) and the 2-4 read chunk offsets are lane constants (token%8 = ((warp*32+lane)/2)%8) -> compute once per kernel (8 regs) or fold into 8 immediate-offset STS from a per-lane permuted base: -16 instr per lane-tile; drop asm volatile from the pure conversion asms (no side effects) so NVVM may interleave blocks.
levers.analytic_model: fp8 per lane-tile 245 -> ~180 (-27%) if the 3-instr pair exists, else 245 -> 229 (-7%) from hoisting alone; at the observed ~11-14 cycles per instruction the expansion segment scales proportionally: fp8 1.6 -> 1.2 us (or 1.5).
levers.predicted_effect: fp8 period 3.0 -> 2.6 us (-> ~80 us) in the best case, 2.9 otherwise; fp4 gains only the hoisting (-16 of 310, ~-0.09 us). Composes with L2-L4 (the count reduction is orthogonal to the rate fix).
levers.verification: cuobjdump: HADD2.F32 count in the converter body 64 -> 0 and F2FP count halves; LOP3/LEA count for stores 16 -> 0-8; ptxas -v register count stays <= budget.
levers.cost_and_risk: Low; bit-exactness must be re-checked against explicit expansion (the f16 intermediate is exact for E4M3 so any correct f16->bf16 RN convert is bit-identical to the current path).
levers.depends_on: ptxas acceptance check for the packed convert
levers.files_and_functions: csrc/xqa/mhaUtils.cuh convertE4M3x2ToA16 (:376), expandCompressedBlock16WithScale (:559); mha_sm90.cu expandPackedStage store addressing (:2812-2814)

levers.name: L6: Rejected-by-analysis levers: convert once per page; fewer/larger stores; removing the proxy fence; more converter lanes from the IO group at the current register split
levers.mechanism: (a) Convert once per page: tiles partition pages and each page is consumed exactly once per CTA in decode (no q-row reuse in q=1; SPEC_DEC keeps all q rows in one CTA), so there is no redundant conversion to remove. (b) Fewer/larger stores: each lane writes 128 B = 8 x STS.128, the widest store; 4 wavefronts per warp-STS is the hardware minimum for 512 B and the XOR swizzle makes them conflict-free (address formula read); the only way to store less is to not store (L7). (c) Removing fence.proxy.async: D5 requires it before wgmma reads generic-proxy writes, and mbarrier.arrive.release would wait for the same store drain anyway; its 0.45 us is the drain, movable (L3) but not deletable. (d) Extra converter lanes from the idle IO warps: setmaxnreg is warpgroup-collective, so the IO group must be uniformly 24 or 56; at 56 the pool is 128x56+256x56+256x48 = 33792 > 30720; three converter groups at 48 uniform (all 640 threads at 48) is exactly the pool but the record says the converter spills at 48 (unverified). Also 6 warps per operand splits 512 blocks per tile unevenly (2.67 blocks per lane -> 3 rounds, 8/9 efficiency), so the best case is 4 blocks -> 3 blocks per lane = -20% expansion (1.69 -> 1.35) for a layout that cannot be register-funded.
levers.analytic_model: (a) 0; (b) 0 (at floor); (c) 0 (drain is inherent, see L3 for overlap); (d) infeasible at 56/48; feasible only as 5 groups at 48 uniform if expandPackedStage fits 48 without STL (check), yielding at most 3/4 of the expansion segment.
levers.predicted_effect: None recommended; (d) only if a ptxas -v run shows the converter body at <= 48 regs with 0 spill bytes, then fp4 period 3.0 -> ~2.6 us.
levers.verification: (d): ptxas -v (FLASHINFER_EXTRA_CUDAFLAGS=-Xptxas -v) spill bytes for the converter functions at maxrreg 48; cuobjdump STS.128 count = 8 per lane-tile confirms (b).
levers.cost_and_risk: n/a

levers.name: L7: Register-side K decode in the gemm0 warpgroup (RS-GMMA for K only), K converter group re-purposed as 4 more V converters
levers.mechanism: With SWAP_AB gemm0's A operand is K (M=64 tokens x K=16 head dims per wgmma), whose register fragment is 4 x bf16x2 per thread = 2 consecutive head dims for tokens r and r+8 at dim pairs 2c and 2c+8 -- the packed byte order exactly (fp8: LDS.U16 x4 or LDS.32 x2 + extract; fp4: LDS.64 per token row, byte c and c+4, 2-nibble LUT). gemm0 issues wgmma.mma_async RS (A regs, B=Q descriptor) k-step k while decoding k+1 (wgmma is async; m64n8k16 is ~8-16 cycles). No A16 stage write for K, no K STS/LDS.128 round trip, no fence/produced rendezvous for K (gemm0 waits its own cp.async group for the packed rows; A16 pages still land by TMA and are read SS -- the per-page format selects RS vs SS per m-instruction, warp-uniform since a warp's 16 rows are one page). The freed 4 warps double the V converters (lane owns 32 values): V expansion 1.69 -> ~0.9 us, V copy issue halves. Contradicts backends.md's normative 'do not port register-fragment decode into the sm90 GMMA consumer', whose basis was a synchronous decode-then-MMA implementation with byte-wise fp4 reads; this variant is async-overlapped and x2/x8-LUT based, so the rule should be re-derived rather than assumed.
levers.analytic_model: Decode moves 1:1 from converter lanes to gemm0 lanes (fp8: 8 k-steps x [2 LDS + 4 x 5] = ~180 per thread-tile; fp4: 8 x [2 LDS.64 + 4 x (extract 1 + x2 LUT 9) + 4 HMUL2] = ~370 -- x2 LUT is 9/pair vs x8's 6.75/pair because the fragment needs dims {2c,2c+1,2c+8,2c+9}, not 8 consecutive). Critical path: cadence = max(consumer floor 1.94 + D_rs, V period). D_rs = decode issue not hidden behind the 8 wgmmas ~ (fp8 180, fp4 370) x ~2.5 cycles (ILP 2 at 64 regs) - 8 x 12 cycles = ~350 / ~830 cycles = 0.18 / 0.42 us. V period with 8 converter warps ~ 0.9 + 0.3 + 0.3 = ~1.5-1.8 us. Smem traffic per CTA-tile drops ~24 KB (K expand write 16 KB + wgmma A read 16 KB replaced by 4-8 KB packed reads).
levers.predicted_effect: fp8 cadence ~2.1 us -> ~68 us; fp4 ~2.4 us -> ~77 us; mixed ~2.1-2.3 -> 68-74 us. Meets the mixed target (62) only with a shorter consumer chain; FP8 58 / FP4 36 remain out of reach on the issue budget (see budgets: FP4 needs 4.4 IPC).
levers.verification: cuobjdump: WGMMA with register A operands (HGMMA ... R-form) in the gemm0 body for the compressed arms, converter-group STS.128 count for K = 0, gemm0 body PRMT/F2FP counts match the model; TRACE: gemm0 kwait->mma segment grows by D_rs, V converter period ~1.5-1.8 us; ncu smem wavefronts per tile drop ~35%.
levers.cost_and_risk: High: new gmma_impl regA specializations for bf16/half m64n8k16, per-page RS/SS selection inside the unrolled k-loop (must stay compile-time shaped to avoid the multi-hour ptxas seen before), gemm0 register pressure (acc 4 + A frags 8 + decode temps ~20 + softmax state) fits 64 (4-group layout) but not 48; breaks the 'consumer untouched' invariant C5 for gemm0; q>1 (SPEC_DEC) needs the same treatment or stays on the smem path.
levers.depends_on: L4 (64-reg budget) and L1 (if the converter is MIO/drain-bound, RS-K removes exactly that class for K; if ALU-bound it only rebalances)

levers.name: L8: Cheaper copy-issue chain (test_wait fast path, precomputed page bases)
levers.mechanism: issueKCopies(t+2) starts with kBar[(t+2)%3].consumed.wait_parity, which is essentially always already complete (gemm0 released tile t-1 before waiting on produced(t)); a try_wait with the max suspend hint still costs a ~150-200 cycle SYNCS round trip. Use test_wait.parity (non-blocking, ~30 cycles) and only fall into the try_wait loop on failure. Precompute this warp's page payload/scale base pointers for tile t+2 during the expansion's initial LDS latency window (the 64-bit IMAD chain and the two dependent LDS of tag/page then leave the critical chain).
levers.analytic_model: Dependent chain ~250-300 cycles uncontended today; removing ~150 (TRYWAIT) and ~60 (LDS->LDS->IMAD) leaves ~80-100; at the observed 4-5x contention factor that is ~0.15 us instead of 0.64 -> ~-0.4 us if the chain is latency-bound, ~-0.1 us if it is LSU-queue-bound (L1 decides).
levers.predicted_effect: fp4 period 3.0 -> 2.6-2.9 us; largely subsumed by L3's overlap, so take L3 first and keep this only if the copy issue remains exposed.
levers.verification: TRACE segment 8->9 shrinks; SASS: SYNCS.PHASECHK without the retry BRA on the fast path; LDGSTS count unchanged (2/4 + 1 per lane).
levers.cost_and_risk: Low.
levers.files_and_functions: mha_sm90.cu issueKCopies/issueVCopies lambdas (:2080-2145), issueCompressedPageCopies (:2538)

open_questions: No SASS instruction count of expandPackedStage exists in the record; the source-derived counts here (fp4-bf16 ~310, fp8-bf16 ~245 per lane-tile) contradict the backends.md estimate (200 vs 100) and explain the 'same 1.6 us' -- confirm with cuobjdump -sass (expect 96 PRMT + 32 HMUL2 + 8 STS.128 for fp4; 64 HADD2.F32 + 64 F2FP + 32 HMUL2 for fp8-bf16).

Per-PC stall reasons for the converter warps are unknown (the recorded 45% selected/not_selected/long_sb is the spinners'); the 4-5x uniform slowdown of both converter segments needs ncu PC sampling restricted to the converter code range before choosing between rate levers (L3/L4) and count levers (L5/L7).

The nanosleep rejection is not conclusive: 'sleeping = 0.00' with issue-active rising 58 -> 66% is inconsistent with a poll loop that actually executed NANOSLEEP; the sm90 poll (barriers.cuh poll<true>) has no sleep, so the tested binary may not have changed the loop. Since try_wait with the max hint suspends in hardware, spinners probably consume PC samples, not issue slots -- consistent with the converter being self-stalled rather than starved.
Does ptxas accept a packed f16x2->bf16x2 (or bf16.f16) cvt for sm_90? It decides whether FP8-bf16 decode is 3 or 5 SASS per pair (L5).

Does expandPackedStage really spill at 48 registers (the comment at :1249 asserts it; no ptxas -v figure recorded)? It decides whether a 5-group / 48-uniform layout with 6 converter warps per operand is admissible (L6d).

GEMM groups run at the launch-bound 48 registers with no setmaxnreg; whether the consumer skeleton is register-serialised at 48 (part of the 1.94 us floor) is unmeasured -- the 4-group layout (64 regs) would answer it via SASS diff of the gemm0/gemm1 bodies.

SPEC_DEC mixed builds fall back to nbKBuf = nbVBuf = 2 (:181, :207: '(ENABLE_MIXED_KV_CACHE && !SPEC_DEC) ? MIXED_KV_KDEPTH : 2') so kAhead = 1 and cp.async landing (~1.9 us) is exposed every tile in addition to the 226-register spill; the q=4 pathology has two causes, only one of which is register pressure.

Analytic feasibility: at 2 CTAs/SM the FP4 target (36 us = 2228 cycles per tile) needs ~4.4 IPC for the software E2M1 decode floor (~2000 warp-instr per CTA-tile) plus the current consumer skeleton (2100); the hardware maximum is 4.0 and the measured is 2.78. No converter-side lever reaches it; FP8 58 us needs ~2.3 IPC and a consumer chain below 1.8 us/tile. The reachable band from the converter side alone is 65-80 us (L2+L3+L4, or L7).

levers.name: L1 Bytes per DRAM request for K: 128 B K parts on sm120 (or FP8 double-part packed loads into a 3-deep K ring)
levers.mechanism: Today a compressed K part request is 32 B (FP8) / 16 B (FP4) per token at 1 KB / 512 B token stride, four separate requests per row spaced P ~1.3-2.8 us apart (row closed in between). Option A: set preferedKHeadPartBytes = 128 for __CUDA_ARCH__ 1200/1210 (mha.cu:121-131), i.e. the sm80/sm90 setting: K part = 64 tok x 128 B A16 (8 KB), FP8 64 B/token (2 contiguous sectors), FP4 32 B/token (1 full sector), 2 parts per head; kSliceRows/gemmKSplit adapt automatically (gemmKSplit 4, 32 HMMA per part). smem: K 4x2x8 KB = 64 KB -> 114 KB total > 99 KB, so pair it with cacheVTileSeqLen = 16 on sm120 (V 4x2x2 KB = 16 KB; gemm1 does 2 V iters per X tile: nbCacheVTilesPerXTile = 4, nbVItersPerXIter = 2) -> ~98 KB (static_assert(smemSize < 99 KB) decides). Option B (keeps 64 B parts and V): for FP8/FP4 tiles copy the packed rows for parts {2j, 2j+1} in one 64 B (FP8) / 32 B (FP4) request per token into K buffer X, expand in place into X (part 2j+1, last) and into a second free buffer Y (part 2j); requires nbKBuffers = 3 (+16 KB -> ~98 KB) and a rotation cur/next/landing.
levers.analytic_model: Request-rate model: time = requests / R_max. FP8 K requests per SM-tile 1024 -> 512 (Option A: 256 tok x 2 parts; Option B: 256 x 2 double-parts), each a full 64 B; with V (1024) and scales (1024 L2, ~128 DRAM) FP8 falls to ~1.3-1.5K DRAM sectors per SM-tile from ~2.1-2.6K, i.e. 4.3-5.5 us per CTA tile at the observed 250-300 requests/us -> 70-90 us, but then the byte roofline binds: 152 MB / 1.58 TB/s (A16's achieved) = 96 us. Mixed: K requests A16 pages 0.74M -> 0.37M (Option A only), FP8 0.66M -> 0.33M, FP4 0.33M -> 0.33M (now full sectors) -> byte-bound at ~1.5 TB/s -> ~115 us. FP4: K 1024 -> 512 full-sector requests; ~1.3K requests per SM-tile -> ~68 us (request-bound still, bytes would allow 51).
levers.predicted_effect: FP8 139 -> ~96-105 us (target <= 125); mixed 146 -> ~110-120 (target <= 135); FP4 84 -> ~68-75 (target <= 79); A16 unchanged (its K requests are already 64 B) or slightly better with 128 B parts (Option A). Under the per-SM-latency reading instead: Option A halves K wait events per tile (2 parts instead of 4, same bytes in flight) -> ~10%; Option B ~5%.
levers.verification: cuobjdump -sass: LDGSTS count per K part halves (Option A: 8-byte copies become 16-byte, count per lane per tile drops from 52 to ~20); ncu dram__sectors_read.sum for FP8 drops ~35-40% at constant dram__bytes_read.sum; dram__throughput rises to >= 85% of peak (byte-bound signature); per-CTA-tile clock64 trace (new hook in mha.cu mirroring MIXED_KV_TRACE) shows P_K falling from 2.17 us to <= 1.5 us; 34/34 bit-exact via tests/attention/run_xqa_mixed_page_transport.py.
levers.cost_and_risk: Option A is a constant change plus V-tile retune; risk is the 99 KB budget (kScales/vScales/rowmax must stay <= ~5 KB) and 2x per-warp register pressure in smemQKPartGemm (kSlice 4 InstInMat -> 8) under launch_bounds(256,1) (255 regs available, currently unknown REG count). Option B is a real restructuring of the K ring (three buffers, expansion writes two buffers) with hazard rules to write down first; FP4 whole-row (64 B = 4 parts) would need a 4-deep ring and does not fit, so Option B gives FP4 only 32 B requests.

levers.name: L2 Whole-row V requests: GRP_LOAD_V = 1 for the mixed build
levers.mechanism: With GRP_LOAD_V=0 each gemm1 warp copies its 64-elem half-row per token (A16 128 B, FP8 64 B, FP4 32 B) and the two warps of a group issue the two halves independently. defines.h's own heuristic says group loads are better when warpTile.x * cacheElemSize < 128 B, which is exactly the compressed case (64 / 32 B slices). Setting GRP_LOAD_V for CACHE_ELEM_ENUM 5 makes VSmemBuffer 32 tok x 256 B (whole head) per group (v[2][1][2] = 32 KB, same total), each warp copies 16 whole rows (A16 256 B = 8 sectors, FP8 128 B = 4 sectors, FP4 64 B = 2 sectors contiguous per token), and the existing vBarrier (cp.async.mbarrier.arrive.noinc via commitVTileLoad) + mixedVExpandBarriers protocol (already coded, mha.cu:2062-2072, 3120-3165) synchronizes the pair. copyMixedPartialHeadsAsync<headsPerWarp=16, nbPartsPerHead=1> path already exists (mha.cu:2860-2880).

Also removes half the V LDGSTS instructions per warp (bytes per warp unchanged, 16 B grains instead of 8 B) and the per-part 4 B scale re-reads on V become 1 x 8 B per token per tile.

Same for V (mixedVScaleBytes already 8).

levers.name: L4 Code shape (sm120 analogues of C2/C6): compile-time page index, no dead zero-fill copies, no per-block 64-bit stride math
levers.mechanism: (i) tokenOffset = seqOffset % 16 is provably 0 for K (ctaTile.x, warpTile.x multiples of 16) and for V (cacheVTileSeqLen = 32); with it constant, block iteration i is page i (K) or page i/2 (V) at compile time -> `pages[iteration]` and `formats.values[iteration]` are constant indices: the register-array LDL/STL disappear (118-168 LDL in the static kernels, 338 in the dynamic one per backends.md). (ii) In the expansion form the `second` grain and the FP4 upper 8 B are overwritten by the expansion, so the 16 B zero-fill cp.async per block (and the 8 B one for FP4) are dead: 13 LDGSTS per part -> 9 (FP8) / 5 (FP4) per lane; the A16 pages inside mixed tiles should use copyAsync<16> x2 per block. (iii) Hoist payloadBase = page*stride.page + head*stride.head per page (warp-uniform per iteration) and use token*stride.token as the only per-lane term; formats span lookup becomes uniform LDC once per iteration.

(b) Overlap: nbKBuffers = 3 (+16 KB, ~98 KB) so expansion of buffer C overlaps MMA of B while A lands; V would need cacheVTileSeqLen = 16 to afford 3 buffers.
